definitions.explanation: The traditional name for the twelfth month. One of the most widely known of the old month names (和風月名). The kanji 師 (master, teacher) + 走 (run) reflect the folk etymology that even Buddhist priests are so busy at year-end that they run around. Still commonly used in modern Japanese, especially in seasonal greetings and media.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}に{入|はい}り、{街|まち}は{慌|あわ}ただしくなった。
examples.english: December arrived and the streets became hectic.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}は{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}やクリスマスで{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: December is busy with year-end parties and Christmas.

examples.japanese: {師走|しわす}の{慌|あわ}ただしさの{中|なか}、{年賀状|ねんがじょう}を{書|か}く{時間|じかん}がなかなか{取|と}れない。
examples.english: In the hectic rush of December, it's hard to find time to write New Year's cards.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The folk etymology is that {師|し} (Buddhist priests/teachers) {走|はし}る (run) because December is so busy with year-end Buddhist ceremonies. While this explanation is widely known, the true etymology is uncertain.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{師走|しわす} is one of the few traditional month names that remains in active everyday use. It evokes the particular busyness of December in Japan: {大掃除|おおそうじ} (year-end cleaning), {忘年会|ぼうねんかい} (year-end parties), {年賀状|ねんがじょう} (New Year's cards), and holiday preparations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {師走|しわす}の{忙|いそが}しさ (the busyness of December)
- {師走|しわす}に{入|はい}る (to enter December)
- {師走|しわす}の{風物詩|ふうぶつし} (things characteristic of December)
